Therefore, the revocation of the Connectivity on the purported basis that the Petitioner failed to meet the aforesaid deadline is not just arbitrary, unconscionable, unjustifiable, and demonstrably high-handed but also lacks any regulatory basis and militates against the established principles of law. Order in Petition No. 809/MP/2025 along with IA 85/2025 and IA 09/2026 Page 6 Order in Petition No. 809/MP/2025 along with IA 85/2025 and IA 09/2026 Page 7 - _(e) The Petitioner is willing to engage its official with CTUIL for clarifying and fulfilling the requirements in respect of land documents submitted on 14.7.2025, 19.7.2025 and 23.7.2025._ - _(a) Without prejudice to its rights & contentions, CTUIL, along with the representatives of the Petitioner, if required, shall examine the revised/ rectified land documents submitted by the Petitioner, within two weeks and shall file its response, along with a reply to the Petition, if any, within two weeks thereafter. The Petitioner may also file its rejoinder, if any, within a week thereafter. The Petitioner and CTUIL shall try to resolve the issues within a given time._ Order in Petition No. 809/MP/2025 along with IA 85/2025 and IA 09/2026 Page 8 _“At the outset, the learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that, pursuant to the previous hearing, the Petitioner furnished the land documents on 22.9.2025, which have been scrutinised by CTUIL and have been found to be in order._ - a) A status quo order was already in operation when the present Petition was reserved for final order on 11.11.2025. However, CTUIL has, in contravention of such _status quo_ order(s) as well as its own submissions on affidavit in the present matter and without any reasonable or regulatory basis, encashed the Order in Petition No. 809/MP/2025 along with IA 85/2025 and IA 09/2026 Page 9 13. During the course of the hearing, the Petitioner submitted grounds for filing the IA 9/2026 after the matter was reserved for Order. After hearing the parties’ submissions, the Commission directed CTUIL to file a reply in the impugned IA and allowed the Petitioner to file a rejoinder. The Commission also directed the parties to maintain the status quo as per the order dated 10.09.2025 until the disposal of the Petition. 21. title: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act 2003 read with Regulations 11A, 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (General Network Access) Regulations 2022 (as amended from time to time), inter alia seeking for quashing/ setting aside of the letter dated 03.09.2025 issued by the Central Transmission Utility of India Limited thereby revoking the 175 MW connectivity granted to the Petitioner under Regulation 11B (1) of the CERC (General Network Access) (First Amendment) Regulations 2023.
